thread.title: Qualcomm: Global 5G Unlocked - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) | Seeking Alpha

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Qualcomm: Global 5G Unlocked - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) | Seeking Alpha
text:
The most important note from the Snapdragon Tech Summit last week is that 5G is a global rollout utilizing Qualcomm ( QCOM ) technology. A lot of the domestic wireless network providers are racing to become the first 5G providers, but anybody just focusing on the domestic market is missing the huge global market converging on 5G while other countries were far behind on 4G.
My very bullish investment thesis on Qualcomm hasn't always included the move to 5G, but the wireless giant is possibly the best positioned company for the global introduction of 5G including the fact that key thorn Apple ( AAPL ) isn't planning a 5G iPhone version until 2020.
Image Source: Qualcomm website
Global Networks The global 4G launch was a slow ramp with most countries far behind the launch of U.S. wireless carriers. Most major economies around the world are now on pace for a 2020 launch. The below slide highlights some of the forecasted 5G launches of European wireless carriers.
Source: Snapdragon Tech Summit 2018
One of the most notable 5G launches is from Vodafone ( VOD ). The global wireless company was recently discussing 4G rollouts in Europe and 3G in India to suddenly have 5G plans in Europe for 2019/2020.
According to Qualcomm, 4G LTE began with limited OEMs, operators and cities. In contrast, the initial 5G launch has a global rollout from the U.S. to South Korea to China with more than 20 global operators.
Source: Snapdragon Tech Summit 2018
While 4G was a long ramp over the last decade, 5G will have a big burst of activity by 2020.
Phone Royalties Another key aspect of the 5G launch are the phone royalties and modem chipsets. The recent confirmations from key global phone suppliers of Samsung and Apple further highlight the growing advantage of Qualcomm in the next cycle.
Samsung expects to launch the Galaxy S10 5G version around March for both the Korean and U.S. markets while Apple doesn't expect to launch the 5G iPhone until 2020. Apple has historically delayed implementing new technologies until gaining scale and efficiency to lower the costs and increase the quality of the product.
The big difference this time around is the global launch so the company faces substantial market loss with the switch to Intel ( INTC ) modems. Apple faces entering the market far behind Samsung and other phone suppliers around the globe with inferior modems and related technology.
The advantage to Qualcomm at this stage is the ongoing royalty lawsuit with Apple. Regardless of how the lawsuit turns out, Qualcomm will have 5G market leadership and collect royalties and sell modems to the vast majority of the 5G phones hitting the market. Apple won't be able to enter the market without paying an estimated $7 billion in outstanding royalties.
Along with the FQ4 earnings call back in early November, Qualcomm updated the 5G license agreement to over 20 companies now signed up to pay royalties to the wireless technology leader.
In total, we are working with more than 18 OEMs who have committed to launch 5G handsets in 2019 based on our 5G and our X50 modems... Our number of 5G licensing agreements is growing, with more than 20 agreements signed to date based on our previously-announced 5G licensing framework, including Meizu and Motorola Lenovo, and we have significantly more manufacturers in discussions for 5G agreements and amendments, positioning QTL for stability as the 5G transition gains momentum.
Even better, Qualcomm is positioned to gain content from the technology complexity of 5G. Some of the technology leadership is why OEMs are lining up to sign deals with the wireless technology leader having no choice but to go along with their demands in order to deliver 5G devices.
Furthermore, 5G brings an order of magnitude increase of complexity over 4G across spectrum, network dark architecture, RF front-end, device form factors, especially the millimeter wave frequencies, power consumption and application and AI processors. This complexity plays directly to Qualcomm's strength as an innovator and systems provider...In 5G, we are well-positioned with design wins at all our key Snapdragon 800 customers. The added complexity of 5G is also driving additional RF content per device, including combinations of sub-6-gigahertz and millimeter wave. As an example, a large number of 5G smartphones in the United States will require millimeter wave capabilities at launch.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that Qualcomm is the best positioned technology company to play the global launch of 5G. The company already was on a path to a $7 EPS estimate (assuming an eventual settlement with Apple) and the prospects for 5G should launch Qualcomm into growth mode for several years.
The stock remains far too cheap down below $60.
